claims.text: The baseline EHEA is in an as-cast state without specific microstructural refinement.
Directional solidification can induce a nanoscale lamellar structure in an EHEA.
Controlled cooling rates and thermal gradients can produce a uniform nanoscale lamellar structure.
The induced nanoscale lamellar structure consists of alternating phases with differing mechanical properties.
Refined lamellar microstructural features increase strength through a Hall-Petch-type effect.
Phase-boundary-mediated plasticity in the nanoscale lamellar structure improves ductility.
Crack deflection by the nanoscale lamellar structure improves ductility.
Directional solidification will increase yield strength by at least 20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
Directional solidification will increase elongation to failure by at least 15% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The proposed strength-ductility improvement should hold for eutectic compositions with compatible phase constituents capable of forming nanoscale lamellae during directional solidification.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements depends on alloy composition and processing parameters.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 20% strength increase and a 15% ductility increase, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only if there is no simultaneous increase. Thus, smaller positive changes could fail the stated quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
